spec_notes: The specification states every stated requirement (C-1..C-42) and marks most open points with "Open:" lines (PORT handling, malformed saved JSON, id range, member-list edge cases, error-status precedence, crash recovery). It decides some unsaid points in ordinary lines sourced "request": C-21 rejects negative and fractional shares and C-14 rejects string cents, although the request only says zero is allowed and the total is checked. Discovery clauses pin choices another correct build need not share: C-46 accepts number spellings such as 10e-1, C-47/C-49 pin id-length handling and upgrade compatibility, C-43/C-48 pin failed-write behaviour. C-45 pins __proto__-style member names. The file repeats a "## Use cases" / "## Clauses" heading pair for the cycle-3 additions. No contradiction of the request found.
tests_notes: Tests are large multi-behaviour scenarios: "rejects invalid submissions without changing data or consuming a number" covers 404s, about 15 rejection cases, malformed bodies and numbering; "commits overlapping mutations once each and resumes the ledger after restart" covers concurrency, numbering, cross-group creation, file validity and restart. Tied to internals: the two failed-write tests preload a patch of fs/promises.rename aimed at DATA_FILE, so a build that writes the file directly would not be blocked and those tests would fail; "long IDs already saved..." and "reopens and appends to a ledger in the original snapshot format" hand-write this build's ledger layout ({groups:[{id,members,expenses:[{payer,cents,shares:[...]}]}]}). Tests that would fail on another correct build: the 16 KiB id limit with 400 above it ("accepted group IDs fit all three routes using a single encoded segment"), acceptance of 10e-1 and 1.0 and rejection of 1.00000000000000001 ("checks whole cents using the wire value and handles member names as own keys", "accepts equivalent JSON number spellings for amounts and exact shares"), and the rejected-creation test requiring status 500. Malformed-JSON requests are sent without asserting their status. No timing dependence seen.
maintainer: The whole-cent check re-parses the raw body to keep each number's source text (JSON.parse context.source, with a regex fallback for older Node), which is easy to break when touching body handling. Every mutation rewrites the full snapshot through one promise queue and swaps the in-memory map only after the rename, so changes to the write path must keep that order and the strict loader in loadGroups in step with the saved layout, which tests also hand-write.
